provenance.sourceText: §16 Abs. 6 UStG: "Werte in fremder Währung sind zur Berechnung der Steuer und der abziehbaren Vorsteuerbeträge auf Euro nach den Durchschnittskursen umzurechnen, die das Bundesministerium der Finanzen für den Monat öffentlich bekanntgibt, in dem die Leistung ausgeführt oder das Entgelt […] vereinnahmt wird." This provision converts foreign-currency amounts for computing the TAX (the periodic VAT RETURN), never for the invoice document itself; §14 Abs. 4 UStG (the invoice's own mandatory-content list) names no currency-conversion requirement at all.

rule.notes: Researched conclusion, not a gap: §16 Abs. 6 UStG's own conversion rule (BMF monthly average rate, for the month of supply) reaches only the periodic VAT declaration a company files, never a value printed on the invoice document a buyer receives. Nothing in §14 UStG's own mandatory-content enumeration requires a converted VAT or taxable-amount line on a foreign-currency invoice. `rateSource: 'none'` reflects that this codebase never needs a German rate for THIS feature. The BMF monthly rate would be a real, separate input for a German company's own periodic-return computation, which is out of scope for #517 (an invoice-printing concern).
